title: Prior Authorization and Admission Notification Schedule — Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing)
content:
Whether a Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) needed prior authorization, how quickly an urgent or emergency admission had to be notified, and whether a retroactive authorization can still be requested all follow the payer class.

| Payer class | Patient classes that need prior authorization | Admission notification (business days after an urgent or emergency inpatient admission) | Retroactive authorization accepted within (calendar days after the date of service) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial PPO Claim | inpatient, outpatient surgery, outpatient diagnostic | 2 | 14 |
| Commercial HMO Claim | inpatient, outpatient surgery, outpatient diagnostic, recurring outpatient, observation | 1 | 0 (never accepted) |
| Marketplace Exchange Plan Claim | inpatient, outpatient surgery, outpatient diagnostic | 2 | 14 |
| Medicare Advantage Plan Claim | inpatient, outpatient surgery, outpatient diagnostic, recurring outpatient | 1 | 14 |
| Original Medicare Claim | outpatient surgery | 0 | 0 (never accepted) |
| BadgerCare Plus (Wisconsin Medicaid) Claim | inpatient, outpatient diagnostic, recurring outpatient | 2 | 30 |
| Wisconsin Workers' Compensation Claim | inpatient, outpatient surgery, outpatient diagnostic, recurring outpatient | 3 | 30 |

**Emergency services (every payer class):** emergency services never require prior authorization and are never denied for lack of it.

Example (hypothetical): an observation stay billed as a Commercial HMO Claim falls in a class that needs prior authorization, and a retroactive request is not accepted for that payer class at all.
